_comment: R5-G18-1 seed catalog: the rolling-release checksum parser in LinuxDistroCatalog (checksumRecordFilename + filenameFromChecksums). Pure, boundary-rich, security-relevant (a surviving mutant that lets a path or a non-record through can splice a bad filename into a download URL). Run: python scripts/run_mutation_test.py scripts/mutation_catalogs/linux_distro_catalog.json

mutants.why: A '#' comment line has parts.at(0) starting with '#', which fails the hex-digest guard below, and a whitespace-only line yields <2 tokens; so both the empty and comment cases are also rejected downstream. The early return is defense/clarity, not the only rejection -- same output for every input.
A real '<digest> <file>' record has exactly 2 tokens; <=2 rejects it.
Inverting the digest guard rejects valid digest records and accepts prose.
&& only rejects a name containing BOTH separators, so a name with just '/' (or just '\') slips through. testFilenameFromChecksumsRejectsPathEvenWhenPatternPermits pins each separator independently.
An empty pattern must disable discovery; inverting builds a match-all regex and returns the first record.

Dropping the '!' makes a VALID pattern (the normal case) early-return {}, so every real discovery returns empty -- the Kali/Debian tests catch it. (Not equivalent: the harness disproved that first guess -- an invalid pattern is rare, but valid patterns are the common path.)
A full match starts at 0; != 0 rejects every valid match so nothing is ever returned.
A full match spans the whole filename; != rejects every valid match.
